title: incident-router: ~70% -> ~90%
baseline_note: Sonnet, medium effort, the one-paragraph prompt from the original PR.

rounds.name: v1-step-by-step
rounds.hypothesis: Generic reasoning boilerplate helps everywhere. (No error-analysis evidence; included because someone always proposes it.)

rounds.name: v2-queue-defs
rounds.hypothesis: Error analysis: most ambiguous-owner alerts go to the team whose service shows the symptom (payments-api pool exhaustion -> payments). Define queues by owned resource.

rounds.name: v3-fewshot-failures
rounds.hypothesis: Paste 60 current dev failures with their correct labels as few-shot examples. (The anti-pattern: block_leaks is off for this demo.)

rounds.name: v4-tiebreak
rounds.hypothesis: Error analysis: multi-component alert chains are routed to the first component LISTED, not the earliest failing. Add an explicit timestamp tie-break rule.

rounds.name: v5-owner-tool
rounds.hypothesis: Error analysis: codename services (svc-orion, svc-vega) are guessed. No prompt can fix missing knowledge; give the model a lookup_owner tool over the service catalog.

sweep.name: v6a-effort-low
sweep.hypothesis: Effort sweep: low. Cheaper; does accuracy hold?

sweep.name: v6b-effort-high
sweep.hypothesis: Effort sweep: high. Remaining failures are multi-signal alerts that need inference.

sweep.name: v6c-effort-xhigh
sweep.hypothesis: Effort sweep: xhigh. If high helps, does xhigh help more?

sweep.name: v6d-effort-max
sweep.hypothesis: Effort sweep: max. The top of the range.
